decision.q: What tells Switchboard the agent needs you?

unsure.where: Claude Code hooks guide; switchboard/app/Switchboard/ImageLinks.swift:231-300 (finding a Claude session).
unsure.why: Claude Code has notification hooks for exactly this (permission_prompt when a tool needs approval, idle_prompt after 60 s waiting), and Switchboard already finds Claude sessions by process id. But "idle" isn't "needs you": an agent idles when it has finished too. And other agents won't have the same hooks.

why: Two signals, and only one drives the badge. The badge counts explicit cards the agent posted (switchboard board add): real decisions, never chatter. The hook becomes a quiet second signal: a dot on the project's tile saying "the agent is waiting", without raising the count. That follows Linear's agent states, where "awaiting input" is something the agent declares.
It also avoids the anti-pattern every precedent warns about: notification fatigue.

title: Can Switchboard tell when the agent is waiting on you?
